scope: Targeted review of future-context simulation, prompt-and-refine, emission regularization, partial rewriting, semantic and temporal distillation, and adaptive waiting. Not exhaustive; no novelty certification.
selection: Started from user-named ZeroPrompt, CUSIDE, CUSIDE-T and FastEmit; followed methods, citations and closely related 2024-2026 work. Existing P01/P02 are cross-references, not duplicate additions.
source_policy: Rely on full PDFs, publisher or arXiv metadata, and author-linked repositories. Search snippets are discovery aids. Source dates can denote first arXiv submission or the conference opening date, as annotated in the catalog.
reproduction_status: PDF retrieval, text reading and selected visual inspection only. No author model, benchmark, training or speedup reproduced. Existing A2/A3 artifacts unchanged.

recorded_search_queries.service: Consensus discovery; conclusions checked against primary sources

search_log_note: Recorded queries are a subset of the performed searches and direct source lookups, not a complete search export or a systematic-review protocol.

source_files.title: ZeroPrompt: Streaming Acoustic Encoders are Zero-Shot Masked LMs
source_files.evidence_location: PDF pp. 2-4, Figures 1-3, Section 3.1, Table 1 (p. 3), Table 2 (p. 4)
source_files.evidence_en: Table 1, LibriSpeech test-clean, 640ms chunk and 0 to 640ms prompt: TDT-F 1136 to 662ms, TDT-L 7328 to 7098ms; greedy/rescored WER stays 4.41/3.80%. Greedy RTF increases 0.04826 to 0.07006. PER-A is 10.4%.
source_files.code_note: WeNet baseline toolkit/checkpoints are identified in the paper. A separate exact ZeroPrompt implementation was not confirmed; no code or checkpoint was run here.

source_files.title: CUSIDE: Chunking, Simulating Future Context and Decoding for Streaming ASR
source_files.evidence_location: PDF pp. 2-4, Figure 1, training objective, Tables 1-3 (p. 4)
source_files.evidence_en: AISHELL-1, Table 3: CTC-CRF/WFST system at 400ms chunk plus approximately 2ms simulation reports 5.47% CER, or 4.79% with NNLM rescoring. Simulation timing uses a GTX 1080. Tables 1-2 test stochastic-context and chunk-jitter training.
source_files.code_note: The official CAT changelog identifies a CUSIDE implementation. Exact recipe/checkpoint reproducibility was not exercised.

source_files.title: CUSIDE-T: Chunking, Simulating Future and Decoding for Transducer based Streaming ASR
source_files.evidence_location: PDF pp. 2-4, Figure 1, joint objective, Tables 1-2 (p. 4)
source_files.evidence_en: AISHELL-1, 400ms chunk: adapted U2++ versus CUSIDE-T beam CER is 6.11 versus 6.02%; with LM rescoring, 5.74 versus 5.51%. CUSIDE-T labels its latency 400+2ms, with another roughly 50-100ms for rescoring. WenetSpeech 10k-hour tests are also reported.
source_files.code_note: The paper points to CAT for code, scripts and checkpoints. Their specific release was not downloaded or reproduced in this review.

source_files.title: FastEmit: Low-latency Streaming ASR with Sequence-level Emission Regularization
source_files.evidence_location: PDF p. 3, gradient equations and Section 3.2 latency definition; p. 4, Tables 1-3
source_files.evidence_en: Table 1, LibriSpeech ContextNet-L: test clean/other WER 4.4/8.9 to 3.1/7.5%, PR90 210 to 30ms. Table 2 shows that stronger regularization can eventually worsen WER.
source_files.code_note: Lingvo is the implementation toolkit named in the paper. An exact runnable FastEmit recipe/checkpoint was not confirmed here.

source_files.title: TrimTail: Low-Latency Streaming ASR with Simple but Effective Spectrogram-Level Length Penalty
source_files.evidence_location: PDF Section 2, Algorithm 1; Tables 1-3 and Section 3 latency discussion
source_files.evidence_en: AISHELL-1 Conformer CTC, 640ms chunk, maximum trim 50: LTD50 210 to 60ms; greedy/rescored error 5.81/5.05 to 5.83/5.09%. The paper also evaluates LibriSpeech and transducers.
source_files.code_note: The paper links the WeNet spectrim pull request; its public page was checked. No training or author result was reproduced.

source_files.title: Improving Streaming Speech Recognition With Time-Shifted Contextual Attention And Dynamic Right Context Masking
source_files.evidence_location: PDF pp. 2-4, TSCA/DRC methods, Table 2 and Section 4.2
source_files.evidence_en: LibriSpeech 960h, CTC/attention system: Section 4.2 reports average test clean/other WER 4.74/12.23 to 4.44/11.62% for one paired group of configurations. The RTF denominator is c, not c+r.
source_files.code_note: An exact author implementation and checkpoint were not confirmed in this bounded review; this is not evidence that they do not exist.

source_files.title: CUSIDE-array: A Streaming Multi-Channel End-to-End Speech Recognition System with Realistic Evaluations
source_files.evidence_location: Collected v1 PDF pp. 2-4, system diagram and Table 1
source_files.evidence_en: Collected v1, AISHELL-4 Table 1: jointly trained multi-channel baseline CER 36.68% at 400ms; real right context 32.51% at 800ms; simulated future context 35.96% at 402ms.
source_files.code_note: Official CAT recipe documentation was located and its public page checked. No model was run.

source_files.title: Delay-penalized transducer for low-latency streaming ASR
source_files.evidence_location: PDF Eq. (19), Table 1; Figure 3 total-latency discussion
source_files.evidence_en: LibriSpeech Conformer, Table 1: lambda 0 to 0.003 changes clean WER 3.40 to 3.70% and mean alignment delay 373 to 102ms; other WER 8.66 to 9.35%, delay 374 to 137ms.
source_files.code_note: The paper identifies k2 implementation support. Exact recipe and checkpoint behavior were not reproduced.

source_files.title: Minimum latency training of sequence transducers for streaming end-to-end speech recognition
source_files.evidence_location: PDF Sections 2-3, Tables 1-2 and latency definition
source_files.evidence_en: WSJ eval92, causal Conformer, no LM, means of three independent seeds: baseline WER 12.1% and PR90 220ms; minimum-latency training 12.8% and 27ms; FastEmit comparator 12.7% and 67ms.
source_files.code_note: An exact author implementation and checkpoint were not confirmed in this bounded review; this is not evidence that they do not exist.

source_files.title: Partial Rewriting for Multi-Stage ASR
source_files.publication: arXiv preprint; venue not independently confirmed in this review
source_files.evidence_location: Collected 15-page v1, Sections 2-4, Algorithm 1 and Table 1
source_files.evidence_en: The paper evaluates partial word error, emission latency and flicker across multiple test sets. Table 1 shows that quality and revision behavior must be assessed together; Sections 2.2-2.3 define the metrics and merge rules.
source_files.code_note: An exact author implementation and checkpoint were not confirmed in this bounded review; this is not evidence that they do not exist.

source_files.title: Analyzing the Quality and Stability of a Streaming End-to-End On-Device Speech Recognizer
source_files.evidence_location: PDF p. 2, Section 2 and Table 1; Sections 3-4
source_files.evidence_en: Table 1 illustrates repeated corrections: 11 unstable-word occurrences over 9 final words gives UPWR 1.22; five revised segments in one utterance gives UPSR 5. The study separates normalization and streaming instability.
source_files.code_note: An exact author implementation and checkpoint were not confirmed in this bounded review; this is not evidence that they do not exist.

source_files.title: Adapting Whisper for Streaming Speech Recognition via Two-Pass Decoding
source_files.evidence_en: Earnings-call evaluation, 5800h adaptation: Table 2 gives 17.60/17.30% WER without/with rescoring at 1000ms chunks. Table 3, 12s maximum delay: RTF 0.30 and mean finalize-operation latency 1126ms on four Xeon virtual cores.
source_files.code_note: WeNet is the paper toolkit. A complete exact recipe/checkpoint reproduction was not performed.

source_files.title: SENS-ASR: Semantic Embedding injection in Neural-transducer for Streaming Automatic Speech Recognition
source_files.evidence_location: Collected arXiv v2 pp. 2-5, Eq. (3), Sections 3.1-3.3 and Table 1; LREC publisher metadata separately checked
source_files.evidence_en: LibriSpeech 960h, greedy/no external LM, Table 1: at 160ms chunks clean/other WER 7.55/18.34 to 7.21/17.89%; at 1280ms other worsens 8.39 to 8.55%. TEDLIUM-2 is also evaluated.
source_files.code_note: Official public training/evaluation repository confirmed. No weights were downloaded and no author result was run.

source_files.title: Learning from Back Chunks: Acquiring More Future Knowledge for Streaming ASR Models via Self Distillation
source_files.evidence_location: PDF p. 3, Eqs. (2)-(5) and Table 1; p. 4, Table 2
source_files.evidence_en: AISHELL-1, chunk 12 plus look-ahead 4 (640ms window), no LM: Table 2 feature-distilled test CER 6.8% first pass and 5.9% rescored, versus same-look-ahead baseline 7.1/6.1%. AISHELL-2 is also evaluated.
source_files.code_note: An exact author implementation and checkpoint were not confirmed in this bounded review; this is not evidence that they do not exist.

source_files.title: Delayed-KD: Delayed Knowledge Distillation based CTC for Low-Latency Streaming ASR
source_files.evidence_location: PDF p. 2, Eqs. (1)-(4); p. 3, Section 3.3; p. 4, Tables 1-3
source_files.evidence_en: AISHELL-1, 40ms inference chunks, Table 1: TAB 0 gives streaming/rescored CER 7.02/5.77%; TAB 80ms gives 6.11/5.42%, FTD50 140ms and LTD50 90ms. Table 2 shows degradation when distillation weight exceeds the selected optimum.
source_files.code_note: An exact author implementation and checkpoint were not confirmed in this bounded review; this is not evidence that they do not exist.

source_files.title: Fast-U2++: Fast and Accurate End-to-End Speech Recognition in Joint CTC/Attention Frames
source_files.evidence_location: PDF pp. 2-3, Figure 1, Eqs. (1)-(6); p. 4, Tables 1-3
source_files.evidence_en: AISHELL-1 Table 1, lower/top chunks 4/24 and D2 beta 0.01: lower greedy CER 7.34%, final rescoring 5.06%, FTD50 170ms and LTD50 70ms. The headline 80ms is half the 160ms lower chunk, not final end-to-end latency.
source_files.code_note: WeNet is the toolkit linked in the paper; the exact Fast-U2++ checkpoint/recipe was not separately confirmed or run.

source_files.title: Selective Lookahead for Attention-Based Streaming ASR
source_files.evidence_location: Collected 7-page v1, Sections III-V, Table III (timing subset), Table V (full test-clean), Table VI
source_files.evidence_en: LibriSpeech train-clean-360, full test-clean, Table V: static R=1 gives WER 6.7%, median/p90 860/1298ms; dynamic learned trigger plus stable prefix gives 6.5%, 306/2800ms. Budget B=1 gives 6.8%, 328/964ms. Table III subset RTF rises 0.40 to 0.60.
source_files.code_note: Official repository linked by the arXiv authors confirmed. Code was not executed; the collected PDF has 7 pages although the arXiv comment says 5.
